q1: SELECT name FROM drinker WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT f.bar FROM frequents AS f, serves AS s WHERE f.drinker = drinker.name AND f.bar = s.bar AND NOT s.beer IN (SELECT beer FROM likes WHERE drinker = drinker.name))
q2: SELECT f.drinker FROM frequents AS f JOIN serves AS s ON f.bar = s.bar WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = f.bar AND NOT s2.beer IN (SELECT l.beer FROM likes AS l WHERE l.drinker = f.drinker)) GROUP BY f.drinker

explanation: Q1 requires that a drinker's *all* frequented bars serve only beers they like, while Q2 only requires that *at least one* of their frequented bars serves only beers they like. A drinker who frequents both a 'good' bar (all beers liked) and a 'bad' bar (some beers not liked) would be in Q2's result but not Q1's.
counterexample_dsp: Drinker Alice frequents Bar1 (serves BeerA and BeerB, both liked) and Bar2 (serves BeerA [liked] and BeerC [not liked]). Q2 includes Alice because Bar1 meets the condition, but Q1 excludes her because Bar2 violates it.
